items.defectStatement: The sibling-host branch in website_name removes the first label and compares the remainder without recognizing public suffixes. Unrelated hosts such as forum.co.uk and evil.co.uk therefore match, incorrectly causing the website path to be displayed.
obligations: Return only the website host when the hosts share a public suffix but have different registrable domains, including github.io tenants.
Preserve path display for valid sibling hosts such as www.example.com and forum.example.com.
Preserve existing exact-host and valid parent-host matches.
items.notes: No public-suffix resolver or dependency exists in the repository; adding one requires changes outside the anchor. Merely referencing PublicSuffix would fail. Label-count thresholds or hardcoded suffix exceptions are incomplete; deleting the branch loses valid sibling matches.

items.defectStatement: The fallback in website_name checks only whether the website host is a parent of the instance host. A website on a subdomain of the instance, such as forum.example.com/user for instance example.com, consequently loses its path.
obligations: Include the path when the website host is a subdomain of the instance host, including nested subdomains.
Preserve path display when the website host is a parent of the instance host.
Require a dot boundary for suffix matches and return only the host for unrelated domains.

items.defectStatement: include_website_name lacks the question-mark suffix required for the serializer inclusion hook, so its presence check is ignored. Because website_name also lacks the restriction applied to website, restricted profiles can expose their website host or path through this attribute.
obligations: Omit website_name when the website is blank.
Omit website_name whenever scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true.
Allow website_name for a present website when profile fields are unrestricted.
items.notes: Renaming alone leaves the disclosure defect. The finding supplies the restriction API needed for this local fix. Eight presence/restriction cases passed in an isolated Ruby harness.
